parsed.explanation: The quote shows the write-up deliberately weakens the induction to transversals meeting C. In the recursive step the IH is applied to (F_c, C\{c}), and the restricted IH there only characterizes transversals of F_c that meet C\{c}. A transversal X of F containing c∈C need not meet C\{c}, so the claimed inference 'X traverses F_c, so it contains a corresponding D_{c,k}' fails. The witness is decisive: F={{1,2},{2,3}}, C={1,2}. Restricted lists give only the pattern {1,2}, yet X={1,3} traverses F and meets C without containing {1,2}; also {3} traverses F_1 without meeting {2}. The stated criterion is false as written. (The lemma itself is true and fixable by using the full IH, but the write-up nowhere proves it, so the finiteness/lower_bound mechanism is unproved as written.)
